atoms.text: Segregation is the separation of races. In the late 1870s, Southern states passed laws that made segregation official. People of colour (POCs) had to go to different schools than white people, had to sit in special areas on public transport and weren't allowed to eat at certain restaurants. They were also restricted to low-paying jobs. To escape these laws, many POCs moved to Northern states. This movement was called “Great Migration”. Even though segregation wasn't official in the Northern states, POCs also experienced some form of segregation there: POCs often lived in neighbourhoods that were separated from white people and also had to go to different schools.

atoms.text: Many people, especially POCs, suffered under the segregation laws. That's why they started protests and organized peaceful marches during the 1950s and 1960s.

atoms.text: This is Rosa Parks. She was an activist of the “Civil Rights Movement”.

On the 1st December 1955, Rosa took the bus home after work in Montgomery, Alabama. Because of the segregation laws, Black people like Rosa had to sit in the back of the bus. On this day, a lot of people took the bus.

At the next stop, a white man entered the bus. Because all the seats that were reserved for whites were already taken, the bus driver told the Black people in the back of the bus to give up their seats so that the white man could sit down. While some Black people stood up, Rosa stayed in her seat and refused to stand up.

hint.sound: to refuse something <voice voiceLang='de' voice='m3'>bedeutet etwas verweigern.</voice>

atoms.text: As a result, the bus driver called the police. Rosa was arrested and got a fine for breaking segregation law. Rosa refused to pay the fine because she believed that the law was wrong and not her actions.

hint.sound: fine <voice voiceLang='de' voice='m3'>bedeutet Strafe oder Bußgeld.</voice>

atoms.text: Following these events, several Civil Rights Movement leaders, including Martin Luther King Jr., came together and decided to boycott busses. For 381 days, Black people didn't take the busses in Montgomery. The protest was successful and the Supreme Court decided that the segregation laws in Alabama were unconstitutional.

hint.sound: Supreme Court <voice voiceLang='de' voice='m3'>bedeutet oberster Gerichtshof.</voice> unconstitutional <voice voiceLang='de' voice='m3'>bedeutet verfassungswidrig.</voice>

atoms.text: Until her death in 2005, Rosa Parks continued to fight for civil rights and justice. She got many awards for her activism.
